Pineapple Cheese Ball

By Bella BucchiottiPublished Nov 03, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 9:46
Instaread

This pineapple cheese ball has a creamy Boursin filling with sweet pineapple, a little jalapeño heat and a crunchy toasted pecan crust.

Pineapple might sound unexpected in a cheese appetizer, but its sweetness works beautifully with garlic-herb Boursin soft cheese. In this pineapple cheese ball, a little heat from finely chopped jalapeño contrasts with the sweet tropical fruit flavor. Toasted pecans give the soft cheese a crunchy crust, making it party-ready to scoop up with crackers or slices of baguette.

Why You’ll Love It

I’m all for the kind of appetizer I can get ready before any guests arrive, especially when it’s made of cheese!

Easy to prepare ahead: You can mix the filling in advance and finish the cheese ball closer to serving.
Sweet and savory: The flavors are great with buttery crackers, salty pretzels, sturdy chips or fresh vegetables.
Generous serving size: One cheese ball serves 10 to 12 people as part of an appetizer spread, and it’s a real crowd-pleaser.

Also try my cranberry orange cheese ball, air fryer mac and cheese balls or baby chick mini cheese balls. And save Christmas reindeer cheese ball for the holidays!

Cream Cheese Pineapple Cheese Ball Ingredients

A complete list of ingredients and amounts can be found in the recipe card below.

Cream cheese: It’s important to soften your cream cheese before making the cheese ball, so it mixes in smoothly without leaving firm lumps in the filling.
Garlic and herb soft cheese: Boursin or another garlic-herb soft cheese is ideal for the filling. Let it soften with the cream cheese before mixing.
Crushed pineapple: I like to use canned crushed pineapple because it’s already in small pieces. Drain it very well, then pat it dry with paper towels so excess juice doesn’t loosen the filling. And once you’ve drained it very well, drain it again because it’s surprising how much juice pineapple can hold onto!
Red bell pepper: Finely dice the pepper so you don’t get large chunks interrupting the creamy texture.
Jalapeño: Mince it finely to distribute the heat evenly. How hot the finished cheese ball tastes will depend partly on the pepper itself. You might like to use less if you’re catering for a mixed crowd or there will be kids who will love the cheese ball but not necessarily the spice!
Green onions: Slice them finely so they blend easily into the cheese mixture.
Garlic powder, dried parsley and smoked paprika: These seasonings reinforce the savory flavor and the paprika adds a subtle smoky taste.
Pecans: Chopped pecans make the crunchy crust. I try to remember to watch them closely as they toast because they can scorch fast! Let them cool completely before coating the cheese ball.
Fresh parsley: This optional addition goes into the pecan coating. Chop it finely so it mixes evenly with the nuts.

How to Make a Pineapple Pecan Cheese Ball

For more detailed instructions with weights and measurements, jump to the printable recipe card.

Toast the pecans: Toast the chopped nuts and then let them cool.
Mix the filling: Beat the cream cheese and garlic-herb cheese until smooth. Stir in the drained pineapple, vegetables and seasonings.
Shape and chill: Spoon the mixture onto plastic wrap, form it into a ball and refrigerate until firm.
Add the coating: Mix the pecans with optional fresh parsley. Unwrap the cheese ball and press the coating onto it.

Substitutions and Variations

Different soft cheese: Substitute the same amount of another garlic and herb soft cheese for the Boursin or try another kind of cheese altogether. I often use Philadelphia in cheese ball recipes, either as the only cream cheese or paired with another. Full-fat soft cheese gives you the richest flavor.
Milder cheese ball: Reduce the jalapeño amount if you want less heat, or leave it out altogether.
Orange or yellow bell pepper: Either can replace the red bell pepper. Finely dice it to mix into the cheese ball. Orange and yellow peppers are sweet but if you’d prefer a less sweet one, go with green bell pepper instead.
Pecans in the filling: You can stir some of the cooled toasted pecans into the cheese mixture for extra crunch, reserving the rest for the outside.
Without herbs: Leave the fresh parsley out of the coating and use just the toasted pecans.
Another nut: Roll your cheese ball in chopped walnuts, pistachios or even mixed nuts.
Gluten-free option: Use gluten-free crackers or offer cucumber slices, celery sticks and bell pepper strips. Check that your garlic-herb cheese and seasonings are labeled gluten-free.

Serving Suggestions

Crackers and bread: Buttery round crackers, wheat crackers, rosemary cheddar crackers and toasted baguette slices all work well with the creamy filling.
Fresh vegetables: Offer celery sticks, cucumber slices or bell pepper strips for scooping.
Other appetizers: For a mix of hot and cold options, serve your cheese ball with spinach artichoke stuffed mushrooms, antipasto skewers and some of these warm appetizers.

How to Store

Store: Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Add the pecan coating shortly before serving for the best crunch. Don’t leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
Freeze: Wrap the uncoated cheese ball tightly in plastic wrap, then place it in a freezer bag or airtight container. Freeze for up to a month. I find the cheese can develop a slightly grainier texture if frozen, so I tend to just make what I think I’ll need (and trust me, you’re very unlikely to have any left over!)
Thaw: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then unwrap and add the toasted pecan coating shortly before serving.

Top Tips

Shape through the wrap: Use the plastic wrap to round the cheese mixture instead of handling it directly. It’s less sticky and easier to manage that way.
Press gently: Lightly press the pecans onto any bare patches. Too much pressure can flatten the chilled ball, so be gentle.
Transfer before softening: Move the firm cheese ball onto its serving platter before letting it soften slightly. It’s easier to transfer while it still holds its shape.

Boursin Pineapple Cheese Ball FAQs

Can I make this cheese ball ahead of time?

You can prepare the cheese mixture up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the refrigerator before shaping and coating. Keep the toasted pecans separate until closer to serving so they don’t lose their crunch.

Is this pineapple cheese ball sweet or savory?

It’s a savory cheese appetizer that has some sweetness from the pineapple. The garlic-herb cheese, onions and seasonings mean it’s not a dessert cheese ball.

Should I serve it straight from the refrigerator?

I like to let mine stand at room temperature for about 15 minutes before serving. This softens the cheese a little, so it’s easier to spread without breaking your crackers.

Pineapple Cheese Ball

By: Bella Bucchiotti
This pineapple cheese ball pairs a creamy garlic-herb filling with a toasted pecan crust. A little jalapeño balances the sweetness of the crushed pineapple.
Prep Time: 20 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 0 minutes minutes
Chilling and Resting Time: 2 hours hours 15 minutes minutes
Total Time: 2 hours hours 35 minutes minutes
Servings: 10
Prevent your screen from going dark

Equipment

  • Measuring Cups and Spoons
  • Mixing Bowls
  • Electric Mixer
  • Rubber Spatula
  • Sharp Knife
  • Cutting Board
  • Skillet Small

Ingredients 

  • 16 Ounces cream cheese, softened
  • 6 Ounces Boursin cheese, garlic and herb, or similar brand, softened
  • 1 Can crushed pineapple, 8 Ounces, very well drained
  • ⅓ Cup red bell pepper, finely diced
  • 1 Tablespoon jalapeño, finely minced
  • ⅓ Cup green onions, finely sliced
  • 1 Teaspoon garlic powder
  • ½ Teaspoon dried parsley
  • ¼ Teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ Teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 ¼ Cups pecans, chopped

To Garnish and Serve

  • ¼ Cup fresh parsley, finely chopped, optional
  • Crackers, baguette slices, pretzels, sturdy chips and/or sliced vegetables

Instructions 

  • Toast the chopped pecans in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 4 to 6 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant.
    • Be careful not to let them burn!
  • Transfer the pecans to a plate and allow them to cool completely.
  • Place the softened cream cheese and garlic-herb soft cheese in a large mixing bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy.
  • Add the crushed pineapple, red bell pepper, jalapeño, green onions, garlic powder, dried parsley, smoked paprika and salt. Stir until everything is evenly incorporated.
    • Make sure your pineapple is VERY well drained! I squeeze it in paper towels or a kitchen towel.
  • Lay a large sheet of plastic wrap on the counter and spoon the cheese mixture into the center. Use the plastic wrap to shape the mixture into a round ball, then wrap it tightly. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
    • Chill it until it's firm and set. It may take longer.
  • Combine the toasted pecans with the chopped fresh parsley, if using, on a plate.
  • Unwrap the chilled cheese ball and gently roll it through the pecan mixture, lightly pressing the coating onto the surface. Place the finished cheese ball on a serving platter.
  • Allow it to sit at room temperature for about 15 minutes before serving so it softens slightly.
  • Serve with crackers, pretzels, toasted baguette slices, celery and/or bell pepper strips, or your dippers of choice.
    • I like to offer a selection of dippers, so people can choose their own.

Notes

Shape through the wrap: Use the plastic wrap to round the cheese mixture instead of handling it directly. It’s less sticky and easier to manage that way.
Press gently: Lightly press the pecans onto any bare patches. Too much pressure can flatten the chilled ball, so be gentle.
Transfer before softening: Move the firm cheese ball onto its serving platter before letting it soften slightly. It’s easier to transfer while it still holds its shape.

If you haven’t tried pineapple in a savory cheese spread, this is a tasty introduction. I love the little bit of jalapeño heat and sweet fruit contrast, but you can leave it out and still enjoy that garlic-herb flavor. It’s quick and easy to prepare and you can make it in advance and bring it out when the party’s about to begin. Cheese balls may have been around for years, but they never seem to lose their appeal!

Other Recipes to Try

  • This White Bean Dip would also be very welcome at a party.
  • I often make Italian Appetizers when friends come over!
  • Looking for a hot appetizer idea? Try my BBQ Grape Jelly Meatballs.
  • Cranberry Bites with Brie always disappear quick!
  • Got canned pineapple left over? Whip up my Pineapple Lush for dessert.
